subject: AI & Agents
title: Pre-Training: Learning from the Internet
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pre-Training: Learning from the Internet usable.

hook.text: Before ChatGPT could chat, it read trillions of words from books, websites, and forums.

buildup.text: Pre-training is self-supervised: the model predicts the next token in massive text datasets.

discovery.text: By predicting trillions of next words, it absorbs grammar, facts, reasoning, and even humor.

twist.text: It also absorbs biases, errors, and toxic content from the training data.

climax.text: Pre-training costs millions of dollars in compute. GPT-4 reportedly cost over $100 million.

punchline.text: Read everything. Absorb everything. Good and bad.

quiz.question: What does an LLM learn during pre-training?
options: To predict the next token from massive text datasets
To browse the internet in real time

details.summary: Pre-training is the initial phase where a language model learns from trillions of words of internet text. The model develops general language understanding, world knowledge, and reasoning abilities during this expensive process.
details.whyItMatters: Pre-training creates the foundation of all LLM capabilities. It requires massive compute and data investment, which is why only a few organizations can train frontier models from scratch.
takeaways: Pre-training teaches general language from trillions of text tokens
It is the most expensive phase, requiring massive compute clusters
The quality and diversity of training data shape model capabilities

faq.question: What data is used for pre-training?
faq.answer: Web pages, books, academic papers, code repositories, and other text sources. The data is filtered for quality, deduplicated, and processed into trillions of tokens. Data composition significantly affects the model's strengths.

faq.question: How long does pre-training take?
faq.answer: Training a frontier model takes weeks to months on thousands of specialized GPUs. GPT-4's training cost is estimated at over $100 million. Smaller models can be trained in days on more modest hardware.
